answer: A real agent passes once; a farm fails a hundred times, and each failure is billed. A name without Madderbound soap maker cloth bond is turned away at the counter, and a bond soap makers lodge after soap house inspections is the reason the counter can tell. The ledger counts names, not wishes, and every name on it has paid its own way. Nobody is waved through free: a fare of £12 for the journey to the registry, paid per name is the price, and the wharf never covers it twice. The glacier is on the docket. Every tide is counted once.
